ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, the altitude $AE$ intersects $BC$ at point $E$. If $\frac{1}{2}\angle ABE + \angle C = 45^\circ$, $CE = 5\sqrt{2}$, and the area of $\triangle ABC$ is 20, what is the length of $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw CD $\perp$ BA from point C, intersecting the extension line of BA at point D,\\
thus $\angle ADC = 90^\circ$,\\
since $\frac{1}{2}\angle ABE + \angle ACB = 45^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ABE + 2\angle ACB = 90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle ABE + \angle ACB + \angle ACD = 90^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ACB = \angle ACD$,\\
since AE is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$,\\
thus $\angle AEC = \angle ADC = 90^\circ$,\\
in $\triangle AEC$ and $\triangle ADC$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle AEC=\angle ADC \\
\angle ACE=\angle ACD \\
AC=AC
\end{array}\right.$\\
thus $\triangle AEC\cong \triangle ADC$ (AAS),\\
thus CE$=CD=5\sqrt{2}$,\\
since $S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}\text{AB}\cdot\text{CD}$,\\
thus $20=\frac{1}{2}\times\text{AB}\times 5\sqrt{2}$,\\
thus AB$=\boxed{4\sqrt{2}}$.

Let β = ∠ABE and γ = ∠ACB; since CE lies on CB, ∠ACE = γ. From the text condition, β/2 + γ = 45°, so β + 2γ = 90°. Draw CD perpendicular to line BA, meeting BA or its extension at D. Angle-chase using CD ⟂ BA and AE ⟂ BC to get ∠ABE + ∠ACB + ∠ACD = 90°. Comparing with β + 2γ = 90° gives ∠ACD = γ = ∠ACE. Now right triangles AEC and ADC have ∠AEC = ∠ADC = 90°, equal acute angle at C, and common hypotenuse AC, so they are congruent; hence CD = CE = 5√2. Use the area of △ABC with base AB and height CD: 20 = (1/2)·AB·5√2, giving AB = 4√2.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/tangent route. From the diagram, set E = (0,0), A = (0,h), C = (c,0) with c = CE = 5√2, and B = (-b,0), where b = BE. Then AE ⟂ BC is encoded by the axes. Let β = ∠ABE and γ = ∠ACB. In the two right triangles, tan β = h/b and tan γ = h/c. Put t = tan γ = h/c, so h = ct. The text condition gives β + 2γ = 90°, hence tan β = cot(2γ) = (1 - t^2)/(2t). Therefore b = h/tan β = 2ct^2/(1 - t^2). The area condition gives 20 = (1/2)(b + c)h = (1/2)c^2·t(1 + t^2)/(1 - t^2). Meanwhile AB = sqrt(b^2 + h^2) = c·t(1 + t^2)/(1 - t^2). raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, the altitude $AE$ intersects $BC$ at point $E$. If $\frac{1}{2}\angle ABE + \angle C = 45^\circ$, $CE = 5\sqrt{2}$, and the area of $\triangle ABC$ is 20, what is the length of $AB$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw CD $\perp$ BA from point C, intersecting the extension line of BA at point D,\\
thus $\angle ADC = 90^\circ$,\\
since $\frac{1}{2}\angle ABE + \angle ACB = 45^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ABE + 2\angle ACB = 90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle ABE + \angle ACB + \angle ACD = 90^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ACB = \angle ACD$,\\
since AE is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$,\\
thus $\angle AEC = \angle ADC = 90^\circ$,\\
in $\triangle AEC$ and $\triangle ADC$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle AEC=\angle ADC \\
\angle ACE=\angle ACD \\
AC=AC
\end{array}\right.$\\
thus $\triangle AEC\cong \triangle ADC$ (AAS),\\
thus CE$=CD=5\sqrt{2}$,\\
since $S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}\text{AB}\cdot\text{CD}$,\\
thus $20=\frac{1}{2}\times\text{AB}\times 5\sqrt{2}$,\\
thus AB$=\boxed{4\sqrt{2}}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is the horizontal base; E is located between B and C, A is above E, and AE is vertically connected to BC, indicating AE⊥BC; AB and AC are respectively the two oblique sides of the triangle. Reasoning: Let β=∠ABE, γ=∠ACB. Because E is on BC, ∠ACE=∠ACB=γ. It is known that (1/2)β+γ=45°, therefore β+2γ=90°. Draw an auxiliary line according to the method: from C draw perpendicular CD to line BA, with foot D, then ∠ADC=90°. From CD⊥BA and combined with the angle relationship of AE⊥BC in the figure, angle chasing can obtain β+γ+∠ACD=90°. Comparing with β+2γ=90°, get ∠ACD=γ. Also ∠ACE=γ, so ∠ACD=∠ACE. Now look at △AEC and △ADC: ∠AEC=90°, ∠ADC=90°, ∠ACE=∠ACD, and AC is the common side, so △AEC≅△ADC. Therefore CD=CE=5√2. Taking AB as the base, the height from C to AB is CD, so the area of triangle ABC is 20=(1/2)·AB·CD=(1/2)·AB·5√2. Solving gives AB=40/(5√2)=4√2.
